title: Duck Breast with Cherry Sauce
subtitle: Pan-roasted duck breast with a sweet-sour cherry sauce
excerpt: A restaurant classic made simple at home: duck breasts scored and started in a cold pan to render the fat slowly, then roasted until the skin is crisp and the meat is pink, served with a sharp cherry sauce made from the pan juices.

recipe.sourceNotes: Duck with cherry sauce (canard aux cerises) is a classic of French restaurant cooking and domestic cuisine, exploiting the affinity between the richness of duck fat and the acidity of sour cherries. The dish appears in classic French cookbooks and was particularly popular in French restaurants in Britain during the 1960s and 1970s as part of the French-influenced dining revolution of that period. The technique of starting the duck breast in a cold pan and rendering the fat slowly is the critical step that differentiates a properly cooked duck breast from an under-rendered one with flabby skin. The fat beneath the skin of a duck breast is thick; it must be rendered almost completely before the skin can crisp.

content.text: Score the fat cap in a crosshatch pattern down to (but not through) the flesh: this allows the fat to render from the interior of the cap as well as the surface. Start in a cold, dry pan and let the heat build gradually over 8 minutes so the fat liquefies and renders before the skin crisps. Rest the breasts for at least 5 minutes after cooking; duck rests more dramatically than chicken and will lose more heat, so tent with foil.

items.preparation: fat cap scored in a crosshatch, every 1 cm; at room temperature for 20 minutes
stoned; or use a 400 g tin of stoned cherries in syrup, drained

content.text: Heat the oven to 200 C (180 C fan). Season the duck breasts with salt and pepper. Place them fat-side down in a cold oven-safe frying pan. Place over medium heat and cook for 8 minutes, pouring away the rendered fat once or twice as it accumulates. The skin should be pale gold and the fat nearly all rendered.

Increase the heat to high for 1 minute to crisp the skin, then flip the breasts and sear the flesh side for 1 minute. Transfer the pan to the oven and roast for 8 to 10 minutes for pink duck (57 to 60 C internal). Remove from the oven, transfer to a board, and rest for 5 minutes, covered loosely with foil.

Pour away all but 1 tablespoon of fat from the pan. Add the cherries, wine, stock, sugar, vinegar, and thyme. Bring to a boil and reduce by half, about 5 minutes, until the sauce is slightly syrupy. Taste and adjust the balance of sweetness and acidity. Slice the duck breasts diagonally and serve with the cherry sauce spooned alongside.
